description: A long, straight, low‐relief channel or ditch trending roughly east–west across the upper third of the DTM image. The feature cuts across natural microtopography with uniform width (~5–8 m) and very subtle banks, suggesting engineered drainage rather than natural erosion.

A cluster of rectilinear raised platforms, each about 30–50 m across, forming an approximate grid in the mid-left of the DTM. The edges are remarkably linear and right-angled, characteristic of raised agricultural fields or habitation platforms.

A linear embankment or causeway trending southwest–northeast in the lower left quadrant of the DTM. This feature appears as a raised ridge (~1–2 m high) with adjacent parallel ditches, consistent with water‐management earthworks.

A subtle rectilinear depression detectable in the NIR band (bright signature) just south of the mid-image clearing boundary, aligning with the DTM’s subtle trenches—likely moisture‐retaining anthropogenic soil.
